{
  "claim": "recover_json_object does not apply last-wins duplicate-key recovery to fenced candidates, so a fenced JSON object with repeated keys is not scoreable even though the documented rule says any candidate that parses as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins is scoreable.",
  "expected": "For a fenced candidate such as {\"a\":1,\"a\":2}, recover_json_object returns ({\"a\":2}, (\"a\",)) and k_recovery returns '{\"a\":2}'.",
  "observed": "The code sets parsed = None for the fenced pool, so it skips the candidate and raises RecordError; k_recovery returns NO_OBJECT.",
  "reproducer": "```json\n{\"a\":1,\"a\":2}\n```",
  "source_basis": "A candidate that parses as strict JSON, or as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins, is scoreable; one that does not (a float, for instance) is passed over. Strict JSON refuses duplicate keys.",
  "execution_evidence": "none: no executable oracle",
  "scope": "Fenced JSON objects with duplicate keys",
  "uncertainty": "None"
}
